definitions.explanation: The act of spreading religious teachings or faith, particularly Christianity. Also used more broadly for passionately promoting any belief, philosophy, or cause.

examples.japanese: {伝道|でんどう}{活動|かつどう}に{従事|じゅうじ}する。
{彼|かれ}は{日本茶|にほんちゃ}の{伝道師|でんどうし}として{海外|かいがい}で{活動|かつどう}している。
examples.english: He is active overseas as an evangelist for Japanese tea.

examples.japanese: フランシスコ・ザビエルは{日本|にほん}にキリスト{教|きょう}を{伝道|でんどう}した{最初|さいしょ}の{宣教師|せんきょうし}だ。
examples.english: Francisco Xavier was the first missionary to spread Christianity to Japan.

notes: Composed of {伝|でん} (transmit, convey) + {道|どう} (way, path, teaching). Originally a religious term, now also used figuratively for anyone who passionately promotes something. Common collocations: {伝道|でんどう}する (to evangelize), {伝道師|でんどうし} (evangelist; also used figuratively), {伝道|でんどう}{活動|かつどう} (missionary activity). Not to be confused with the homophones {電動|でんどう} (electric-powered) or {殿堂|でんどう} (hall of fame). Related: {宣教|せんきょう} (mission, propagation of religion) is a near-synonym but more specifically religious, while {伝道|でんどう} extends more easily to figurative use.
